articles.title: Jose Mourinho: Atletico Madrid hit back at Real Madrid boss after referee criticism following derby defeat
articles.summary: Atletico Madrid have hit back at Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho after his criticism of referees following their derby clash on Sunday; Mourinho held up pictures of refereeing errors in his post-match press conference following 2-1 defeat to rivals
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho arrived at the post-match press conference with printouts displaying two incidents he believed should have resulted in red cards to Atletico players.

The former Chelsea manager accused officials of making key errors in the match, which Real lost 2-1.

On Monday, Atletico put two posts on their X account, the first a video showing a sheet of paper being printed with the words '#StopAcosoArbitalYA,' which means "stop referee harassment now".

A second post showed an image of Mourinho at the news conference with the same message.

Mourinho held up pictures of two tackles to the media after Real's defeat.

Mourinho strongly criticised the officials and was angry that Atletico defender Cristian Romero ‌ was not sent off for a stamp on Jude Bellingham .

He also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde , before the visitors were reduced to 10 men five minutes after half-time.

"We could skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," ​Mourinho said, holding up the images in what was the start of a near ‌five-minute rant.

"Those were two clear red cards. The difficulties we've faced since the sending-off - 11 against 10 - well, we can imagine what 50 ​minutes of 11 against nine would have been like if justice had been done."

Real defender Dean Huijsen was dismissed for bringing down Giuliano Simeone inside the area as the last defender, allowing Alejandro Grimaldo to ​score with a low spot-kick.

Jonathan David doubled Atletico's lead six minutes later, ⁠with Antonio Rudiger heading in a free-kick late ⁠on to reduce the deficit.

Mourinho said he could only "hug" his players after what he described as a first half "full of class and great character", but he aimed sharp ‌criticism at referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias and those who appointed him.

"They've put a referee, aged 41, with no international experience - it's certainly not because he's a great referee," Mourinho said.

"Then the poor chap has come ‌here and hasn't been able to cope with the pressure - and it really is intense pressure. I call it '80s-style pressure' here in this stadium, which you hardly ever see these days."

Asked about being six points behind Barcelona, Mourinho offered a pointed reply.

"If they just leave us in peace and let us compete on a level playing field ⁠with everyone else, we've still got a long way to go," he said.

"I don't ​want to go so far as to say this was set up... I ​want to believe that they simply made a mistake."

'A derby marked by poor officiating,' say Real Madrid

Real Madrid also released an official match report after full-time which echoed the views of Mourinho.

The La Liga club claimed the defeat was "marked by poor officiating".

"Real Madrid lost at the Metropolitano in a derby marked by the poor officiating of Ortiz Arias, who failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Jude Bellingham's knee (despite reviewing the play on the monitor) and Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

"Both decisions shaped the match, which was decided in the second half in favor of Atletico.

"Until the 30th minute, the game had very few dangerous plays. But from that point on, controversy took over the derby.

"In the 35th minute, during a contested ball, Bellingham got to the ball before Cuti Romero, and the Atletico defender planted his studs into the left knee of the Madrid player. Ortiz Arias initially booked our player but was called by Trujillo Suarez to review the incident on the monitor.

"After watching the replay, he rescinded the card from Bellingham and issued a yellow card to the Atletico defender instead of sending him off.

"Nine minutes later, the referee made another crucial error by not penalizing Kang-In Lee for a challenge on Valverde, where he struck him with his studs on the left ankle.

"Ortiz Arias was close to the incident but did not show a red card (or even a yellow card) to the Atlético player, nor was he alerted by Trujillo Suárez on this occasion."

images.caption: Image: Real Madrid said the derby against Atletico Madrid was influenced by refereeing decisions

articles.title: Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy will be game-time decision for No. 4 Rebels in showdown with No. 21 Florida
articles.summary: Lacy suffered an apparent shoulder injury during the Rebels' win over LSU, but head coach Pete Golding said it "wasn't nearly as bad" as originally believed.
articles.body:
Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy will be a game-time decision for the No. 4 Rebels as they visit No. 21 Florida on Saturday in another SEC matchup between top-25 teams.

Head coach Pete Golding announced Lacy's status during his Monday press conference, telling reporters ( via the Mississippi Clarion Ledger ) the injury "wasn't nearly as bad as we thought it was."

Lacey rushed for 43 yards on nine carries in Ole Miss' 32-24 win over No. 10 LSU before leaving the game in the third quarter with what appeared to be a left shoulder injury and was announced as "an upper-body injury."

Following the Rebels' victory, Golding told reporters that X-rays on Lacy's shoulder came back negative . The running back wanted to return to the game and play through the pain he was experiencing, but coaches decided to keep him on the sideline as a precautionary measure.

For the season, Lacy has rushed for 191 yards and four touchdowns on 39 carries. Last year, he had a breakout season with 1,567 rushing yards and 24 TDS on 306 carries, adding 177 yards on 29 receptions.

In Lacy's absence, freshman JT Lindsey rushed for 20 yards on four carries. The transfer from LSU will start against Florida if Lacy is unable to play. In three games, he's tallied 48 yards on 12 rushes.

Florida coach Jon Sumrall surprised Gators are a favorite over Ole Miss

Last season, Ole Miss defeated Florida 34-24 with Lacy rushing for 224 yards and three TDs on 31 carries. That performance may be why his potential absence has sportsbooks making the Gators the surprise favorites early in the week.

Despite the big win over LSU and their higher ranking in the AP Top 25 poll, the Rebels are 3.5-point underdogs to the Gators ahead of their matchup.

Informed of that by a reporter at his Monday press conference, Florida head coach Jon Sumrall quipped, " There's a lot of good drugs out there, huh? "

articles.title: Ole Miss football made a leap, but LSU wasn't their 'Super Bowl'
articles.summary: Pete Golding and the Rebels have a tough schedule ahead.
articles.body:
With all the drama surrounding the LSU Tigers football program leading up to last Saturday's game with the Ole Miss Rebels , Lane Kiffin's highly anticipated return to Oxford didn't go as planned.

Kiffin finally faced off against his old squad, but the reunion was spoiled in exciting fashion. Ole Miss showed their old coach he made a mistake by leaving the Rebels right before the team's College Football Playoff run last season.

The Rebels started the game jumping out to an early 24-7 lead at halftime. However, the second half was a different story. The Tigers came roaring back and tied the game at 24 in the fourth quarter. This was the moment that Ole Miss showed the nation who they were.

While being outscored 17-0 before the game-winning touchdown, Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and the offense drove 75 yards down the field to score and successfully converted a two-point conversion to go up by eight points and end the LSU run.

Kiffin gave credit to Chambliss for the victory, labeling him "the hardest player to play in America." He gave credit to the monster he created and even took credit for the stadium being full an hour before kickoff.

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said after the game, "It wasn't the Super Bowl, and we didn't make it to be the Super Bowl."

The Rebels showed just how dominant they can be in a big prime-time game. This was an early glimpse of what the Playoff atmosphere would be like in Oxford with a return run. Needless to say, the Rebels stepped up to the plate, again.

Under Golding, the Rebels won two Playoff games, but that was with Kiffin's roster. Now he could start his own dynasty and do something even greater. Bringing a national championship to Oxford for the first time in 66 years is the ultimate goal.

Golding's comment about the game not being their Super Bowl was precise because of their fierce competition with the rest of the schedule. He knows LSU was the first of many major tests this season.

They still face a revamped No. 21 Florida team next week in the swamp, No. 1 Texas Longhorns in Austin, and No. 4 Georgia at home. The rest of the season will not be any easier for the Rebels.

With Kiffin no longer around calling the shots, beating LSU will either prove to be a stepping stone or a fluke. We'll wait to see what Ole Miss is made of down the stretch.

articles.title: Vote for The Daily Herald's TSSAA football athlete of the Week from Week 5
articles.summary: Vote here to decide The Daily Herald's Columbia area TSSAA football Athlete of the Week from Week 5 of the high school season.
articles.body:
We're through another Friday night in the Tennessee high school football season and there was no shortage of standout performers across the Columbia area in Week 5 .

Now you can cast your vote to decide The Daily Herald's TSSAA football Athlete of the Week.

Nathanel Karkau, Columbia Academy: Karkau caught three passes for 44 yards and a score, and on defense had five tackles and a sack.

Daniel Booker, Columbia Central: Booker completed 12-of-16 passes for 172 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing six times for 75 yards and two touchdowns in a 45-7 win over Lawrence County.

Brody Bullock, Independence: Bullock caught six passes for 114 yards and two touchdowns, while also rushing for a touchdown, in a 56-14 win over Coffee County. On defense he added an interception returned for 27 yards.

Caden Hagan, Loretto: Hagan had 15 carries for 166 yards and three touchdowns in a 35-28 defeat to Collinwood.

Jonah Gipson, Spring Hill: Gipson rushed 12 times for 101 yards and two touchdowns while also completing 6-of-10 passes for 45 yards in a 36-12 win over Maplewood.

McKaleb Powell, Summertown: Powell had 114 all-purpose yards and two total touchdowns in a 30-7 win over Scotts Hill.

Micah Sally, Summit: Sally caught 10 passes for 125 yards and two touchdowns in a 42-21 defeat to Lincoln County.

Cam Surratt, Zion Christian: Surratt was 15-for-21 passing with 270 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in a 43-12 defeat to Christian Community.

Be sure to cast your vote below before the poll closes at noon on Thursday.

articles.title: Infantino apoya la reforma de la FIFA y pide unidad
articles.standfirst: Carta a los miembros del Consejo y a los presidentes de las 211 asociaciones
articles.summary: Carta a los miembros del Consejo y a los presidentes de las 211 asociaciones
articles.body: Gianni Infantino, presidente de la FIFA, más contestado que nunca y con apoyos que van y vienen, mostró este lunes su apertura al diálogo para buscar reformas en la gobernanza del futuro y actualizar así el modelo de la institución del fútbol mundial, en una carta enviada a los miembros del Consejo de la FIFA y a los presidentes de las 211 asociaciones de la organización. En una misiva, a la que tuvo acceso EFE, Infantino explica que durante las últimas semanas, se ha tomado el tiempo de escuchar antes de dirigirse a sus destinatarios por escrito. Sobre todo con el asunto de la privatización de los Mundiales y otras competiciones: "Los procesos democráticos de la FIFA, su independencia y su autoridad deportiva nunca estuvieron en venta. No están en venta ni lo estarán jamás. La reciente propuesta exploraba si una inversión minoritaria en una sociedad comercial controlada por la FIFA podría generar recursos adicionales para ese fin. No contemplaba renunciar al control de la FIFA ni a su autoridad sobre las decisiones deportivas", afirma. Infantino reconoce que la filtración suscitó inquietud y dio la impresión de que ya se habían tomado decisiones. "Seguía siendo una propuesta, no una decisión, y siempre estuvo sujeta a las aprobaciones necesarias del Consejo y de las federaciones miembro. Ahora ha sido retirada y no seguirá adelante", argumenta Gianni Infantino, que está encontrando muchas resistencia en varias federaciones como la francesa para su reelección. Infantino insiste en buscar nuevas formas de ingresos y abre el diálogo no solo al Consejo sino a las 211 federaciones en medio de una situación compleja y convulsa que vive la FIFA tras acabar el Mundial 2026 de EEUU, México y Canadá. Y por último, el presidente de la FIFA manda un mensaje final donde pone en valor la independencia de la institución. "El trato dispensado a ninguna federación dependerá de su posición sobre una propuesta o un asunto institucional. Sigo a disposición de cada uno de ustedes. Todas las federaciones miembro tienen derecho a ser escuchadas. Estar de acuerdo no es una condición para dialogar, y el desacuerdo nunca debe impedir el respeto mutuo. Sigo plenamente comprometido con la dirección de la FIFA y confío en lo que podemos lograr juntos. Nuestra responsabilidad va más allá de cualquier propuesta o desacuerdo concreto. Consiste en proteger la independencia de la FIFA, fortalecer sus instituciones y garantizar que el progreso del fútbol beneficie al conjunto de este deporte, en todo el mundo. El fútbol es para todos, en todas partes. Este principio seguirá guiando nuestro trabajo", apostilla Infantino.

images.caption: Gianni Infantino, en un Congreso de la UEFA. AP

articles.title: Bellingham y su guerra con los argentinos del Atlético: "Con Messi hablas mucho, aquí nada"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista inglés se encaró en varias ocasiones con el Cuti Romero y Giuliano
articles.summary: El centrocampista inglés se encaró en varias ocasiones con el Cuti Romero y Giuliano
articles.body: el derbi del Metropolitano fue caliente y vivió muchos enfrentamientos y situaciones polémicas. Una de ellas fue la que vivió Jude Bellingham durante todo el partido con los argentinos del Atlético de Madrid. Primero con el 'Cuti' Romero y más tarde con Giuliano Simeone. Y así lo destapó "El Día Después" de Movistar, que captó varias conversaciones entre los protagonistas. En una de ellas, Bellingham recuperó viejas rencillas en clave selección -Argentina eliminó a Inglaterra en semifinales en el pasado Mundial- y le mandó un recado al 'Cuti' Romero: "Con Messi hablas mucho, aquí nada". Justo antes, en el inicio de esa conversación, ambos habían intercambiado impresiones: "Eres un cagón", le decía el inglés, mientras el defensa argentino tampoco se quedaba callado: "Llorón, lloraste allá". Al enfrentamiento con el defensa argentino, le siguió otro con Giuliano Simeone tras otra falta. Ambos juntaron cabezas y el jugador rojiblanco fue explícito en sus 'deseos': "La concha de tu madre", mientras Bellingham respondía con el clásico "Fuck you". Dos cara a cara de los muchos que hubo en el derbi del Metropolitano, donde la tensión se hizo presente durante todo el partido y llevó, incluso, a un par de expulsiones en el camino hacia vestuarios en el descanso del partido.

images.caption: El 'Cuti' Romero y Bellingham discuten durante el derbi

articles.title: Embattled Gianni Infantino says he is open to talks over FIFA reform
articles.summary: FIFA president proposes ‘consultation’ with members to reform world football governing body’s decision-making process.
articles.body:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has proposed an outside review of how the governing body makes major decisions, ⁠acknowledging in a letter to members that its handling of a now-abandoned investment plan had caused outrage.

“First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of FIFA’s current governance framework for ⁠major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements,” Infantino wrote to the FIFA Council and all 211 member association presidents on Monday in a letter seen by the Reuters news agency.

He also said he would propose consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders on strengthening FIFA’s decision-making.

The proposals would examine who has a say in major initiatives – including the roles of the president, bureau, ‌council and congress – and how to improve transparency and accountability.

Infantino faced a fierce backlash over his proposal to sell a 20 percent stake in FIFA’s commercial rights, including the World Cup, to private investors. The plan was abandoned in July after opposition and boycott threats, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf subsequently calling for changes to FIFA’s leadership.

Infantino said the abandoned plan had explored whether selling a minority stake in a FIFA-controlled commercial company could raise more money for football development. It would not have involved giving up control over ⁠sporting decisions, he said.

But the proposal became public before it could be presented in ⁠full to the council and member associations, according to Infantino.

“I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not.

“It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals ⁠of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed.”

Infantino said he had heard differing ideas about who should decide major strategic ⁠questions. Some favoured requiring unanimous agreement in the bureau, while others wanted ⁠such matters put directly to the congress and member associations.

“My role is not to pre-judge that discussion. Those who support a particular model should have the opportunity to set out their case clearly,” he wrote.

Suggestions received by the October 15 FIFA Council meeting could be discussed there, with ‌later submissions also considered within a deadline yet to be specified. Any changes to FIFA’s statutes would need congress approval.

Infantino also said member associations’ positions on proposals or governance matters would not affect their treatment by FIFA, whose ‌development ‌and solidarity programmes would continue under existing rules.

“No association’s treatment will depend on its position on any proposal or institutional matter,” he wrote.

“I remain fully committed to leading FIFA and confident in what we can achieve together.”

images.caption: Infantino has faced a fierce backlash over his proposal to sell a ​20 percent stake in FIFA's commercial rights to private investors [File: Beata Zawrzel/AP Photo]

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president open to reform and external review of football's governing body
articles.summary: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates. shifting tone as he seeks support to stay on.
articles.body:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates, and says he is open to reform.

In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino explains the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".

Before a meeting of the Council next month, Infantino says he is also suggesting a consultation on "how Fifa's decision-making can be further strengthened".

This would include proposals on the role of the president, as well as "practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. That would have involved selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, and it sparked a major backlash.

In what appears to be a conciliatory gesture, Infantino writes: "Over recent weeks, I have taken time to listen before writing to you", and says the consultation will be with confederations, member associations and "relevant stakeholders".

He insists that the FFE plan "did not involve relinquishing Fifa's control or authority over sporting decisions. Obviously!"

His letter adds: "The proposal entered the public domain before Fifa's planned institutional process had been completed and before it could be presented in full to the Council and the member associations. I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not."

Infantino also claims that "democratic processes, independence and sporting authority were never for sale. They are not for sale and never will be."

He states he remains "fully committed to leading Fifa and confident in what we can achieve together".

Infantino's letter comes after Uefa and Concacaf - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America and the Caribbean - demanded Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members from its cash reserves.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Infantino claims that the collapse of FFE "does not diminish our ambition or our responsibility to invest more of Fifa's success back into football.

"We will continue to explore sustainable ways to grow Fifa's resources and expand development and solidarity support for every member association," he adds in the letter.

"What changes is not the ambition, but the strength of the process through which major ideas are developed, tested and decided.

"The progress we have made over the past decade gives us a strong foundation for the future. It also gives us the confidence to examine whether our governance remains suited to the scale and complexity of the decisions ahead."

Earlier this month, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, told Infantino to release all documents relating to his controversial plan.

The 56-year-old Swiss-Italian Fifa leader will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Last month, European football's governing body Uefa began preparing criminal legal proceedings against Infantino at courts in the US over the FFE plan, demanding the release of all documents.

Fifa hit back and accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership" in a challenge to the litigation.

Infantino's tone shift represents change in bid to survive - analysis

Having defiantly clung to power for weeks amid an unprecedented rebellion over his presidency, this is a significant change in tone from Infantino - and the first sign that he may feel he has no choice but to compromise if he is to win another re-election in March.

On 15 October, the Fifa Council will meet for the first time since this crisis began, and Infantino will no doubt hope that this relieves some of the pressure he is under.

But even if he is prepared to accept some changes to the way Fifa is run, will that be enough to win over some of those that have turned against him?

As well as wanting him to step down, many of Infantino's critics want an overhaul of Fifa's governance, with curbs on the president's power (such as a maximum of a single term in office), more separation between the president and the Fifa administration, greater emphasis on human rights and sustainability, and the redistribution of Fifa's cash reserves.

It will be fascinating to see if Infantino is prepared to accept such changes if it means staying in power.

images.caption: Image caption, Gianni Infantino was first elected as Fifa president in 2016

articles.title: Gabi, al banquillo del Madrid: "Me vas a comer la p..."
articles.standfirst: Gabi y Rüdiger protagonizaron un tenso cara a cara desde los banquillos, con gestos y palabras subidas de tono en uno de los momentos más polémicos del derbi
articles.summary: Gabi y Rüdiger protagonizaron un tenso cara a cara desde los banquillos, con gestos y palabras subidas de tono en uno de los momentos más polémicos del derbi
articles.body: El derbi en el Metropolitano dejó tensión dentro y fuera del terreno de juego. La polémica también se trasladó a los banquillos, con un enfrentamiento entre Gabi y Antonio Rüdiger que terminó con gestos y palabras subidas de tono en medio de un enganchón que terminaría en el túnel de vestuarios con dos expulsiones (Pablo Vercellone, entrenador de porteros del Atlético de Madrid, y Pedro Machado, segundo de Mourinho). El nuevo asistente de Simeone fue uno de los protagonistas de la discusión desde el banquillo rojiblanco. En un momento de máxima tensión, Gabi se llevó las manos a la entrepierna y realizó un gesto dirigido hacia el sector del Real Madrid. Poco después, las cámaras captaron su conversación con Rüdiger, en un cara a cara que fue elevando la temperatura. Durante ese intercambio, Gabi llegó a lanzar al banquillo blanco en repetidas ocasiones: "Me vas a comer la polla", en una respuesta que refleja el nivel de tensión que se vivió en ese momento tal y como grabaron las cámaras de DAZN. Rüdiger, que parecía mantener una conversación directa con el exjugador rojiblanco, acabó protagonizando el cruce mientras desde el banquillo madridista también intervenía Pedro Machado, asistente de José Mourinho. El ayudante del técnico portugués señaló a Gabi para que regresara al vestuario y dejara de continuar con la discusión. La escena no pasó desapercibida y se suma a los diferentes episodios polémicos que dejó un derbi marcado por la intensidad, tanto sobre el césped como en los banquillos.

images.caption: Imágenes de DAZN del enfrentamiento verbal en el derbi.

articles.title: Ole Miss Players Taunting Lane Kiffin in Photo Goes Viral After New Angle from Win vs. LSU Surfaces
articles.summary: Ole Miss got its revenge win over former head coach Lane Kiffin and his new team, LSU, on Saturday, and Rebels players are still soaking it in.
articles.body:
Ole Miss got its revenge win over former head coach Lane Kiffin and his new team, LSU, on Saturday, and Rebels players are still soaking it in.

On Monday, Jaylon Braxton posted an Instagram photo of himself taunting Kiffin after making the game-sealing interception against the Tigers.

Braxton spent one season under Kiffin at Ole Miss in 2025, so it's hard to imagine how good it felt for him to play hero for the Rebels against Kiffin and the Tigers.

Kiffin was at the helm in Oxford for six seasons and turned Ole Miss into a national championship contender last season before darting for LSU at the end of the season.

His exit set the stage for a hostile environment at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and it ultimately proved too much for LSU as the Rebels picked up a signature win early in the season.

articles.title: Las primeras grietas del plan inicial de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: El duo Valverde-Tchouaméni no genera lo que se esperaba con Bernardo Silva a la espera y Diomande amenaza al tridente
articles.summary: El duo Valverde-Tchouaméni no genera lo que se esperaba con Bernardo Silva a la espera y Diomande amenaza al tridente
articles.body: El derbi sirvió para que Mourinho abandonara su plan conciliador con la Liga con el que regresó al Real Madrid esta temporada, pero también para comprobar cuál era su plan estrella sobre el terreno de juego, algo que por otra parte ya se esperaba antes del choque en el Metropolitano. El once del Real Madrid fue, por otro lado, casi el mismo que cayó de forma estrepitosa la campaña pasada con Xabi Alonso en el banquillo. Solo tres cambios: Dumfries, por Carvajal, Konaté y Cucurella como novedades. En el medio campo y en la delantera, por tanto, los mismos. Y este plan idéntico e inicial de Mou ha confirmado que tiene fisuras. Mourinho, sin embargo, dejó muy claro que le gustó el Madrid en el primer tiempo. La imagen no dice lo mismo porque se vieron problemas de partidos anteriores. Fue en la segunda parte, pese a jugar con uno menos, con la entrada de Diomande y Bernardo Silva, ya con poco tiempo, cuando el Madrid obligó al Atlético a echarse a algo más atrás. El gol de Rüdiger, que también salió desde el banquillo tras la expulsión de Huijsen, fue el premio a la insistencia del costamarfileño por la izquierda, el único que pudo con Giuliano y Marcos Llorente. El entrenador del Real Madrid mantiene a Vinicius, Mbappé y Bellingham como intocables, aunque el brasileño está siendo el primer cambio de los tres. El otro que se ha ganado el puesto es Güler, aunque también es de los primeros en salir. Diomande ya fue el mejor en su segundo partido de titular ante el Elche. También en su debut en el once frente al Rayo en el Bernabéu. Sin embargo, su entrada en el once implica un sacrificado entre estos cuatro jugadores. Por la izquierda, donde Diomande está convenciendo, está Vinicius, pero el fichaje más caro de la historia del Madrid también puede jugar por el costado derecho. Mou ha puesto a Valverde a jugar por dentro al lado de Tchouaméni, que ha tardado en subirse al once, hasta que no se ha recuperado totalmente de su lesión. Güler es el tercer hombre, pero tampoco este tridente está logrando mantener siempre el control del partido. En esta parcela podría entrar Bernardo Silva, un refuerzo que el propio Mou pidió al club al tener constancia que abandonaba el City y con el Atlético al acecho ya que lo veía como el recambio ideal de Griezmann. El luso puede ser una alternativa en esa posición e incluso en el tridente de arriba. Para cambiar el rumbo en el medio campo, Mou tiene las opciones de Camavinga, que ha vuelto a la selección con Zidane, y Thiago Pitarch, que desde el pasado 6 de septiembre ya se entrena con el resto del grupo tras superar su lesión de pretemporada. Ya la campaña pasada, fue uno de los revulsivo de Arbeloa, entonces también en busca de soluciones. En lo que va de campaña, y en un partido con bajas como el del triunfo ante el Inter en Champions, el luso optó por colocar a Trent en la medular.

images.caption: Mourinho, en un momento del derbi del pasado domingo en el Metropolitano. AP

articles.title: Héctor Álvarez, con MARCA tras ganar el bronce: "Ahora me veo con posibilidades de ir a por el oro"
articles.standfirst: El joven ciclista español celebra el bronce mundialista en la crono sub 23, admite que soñaba con el oro y ya mira a la ruta
articles.summary: El joven ciclista español celebra el bronce mundialista en la crono, admite que soñaba con el oro y ya mira a la ruta
articles.body: Héctor Álvarez, ciclista del Lidl-Trek, llegó al hotel de España con un bronce al cuello y el oro todavía rondándole la cabeza tras su gran actuación en la crono sub 23 de la cita canadiense. A los 19 años, la decepción dura poco cuando el horizonte vuelve a vestirse de arcoíris. El español sabía que llegaba al Mundial en un momento dulce. La crono era una de sus grandes oportunidades y la carrera confirmó esas sensaciones. "Veníamos con la intención de ganar, pero hemos acabado con una medalla de bronce. Creo que hay que estar muy orgulloso", explica a MARCA. "Sabía que estaba en un momento muy, muy bueno y que, si todo nos acompañaba, podía estar luchando por el oro. Y así ha sido". El viento terminó condicionando el desenlace. Álvarez reconoce que quizá no administró del todo bien sus fuerzas cuando las condiciones cambiaron. "En la última parte, para los últimos corredores, el viento pegó un poco más y toda la vuelta hacia la salida era con aire de cara. Creo que igual he guardado un poco de menos. Tenía que haber guardado un poco más sabiendo que había aumentado el aire". No busca excusas. "A agua pasada ya se ve todo más fácil. Hay que estar contentos, saber que he hecho el 'pacing' que tenía pensado y han sido mejores. Ya está". Una frase que resume bien cómo encaja el resultado: con ambición, pero también con naturalidad. El Mundial, además, todavía no ha terminado para él. El viernes espera la ruta, una carrera mucho más imprevisible que la contrarreloj. "La ruta es un poco más extra. Pueden pasar más cosas, pero también me veo con posibilidades de luchar por el oro. Hay que estar motivado y, con el equipo que traemos, podemos hacer muchas cosas". Álvarez sabe también que ese tipo de pruebas exige correr sin complejos. "Creo que hay que correr sin miedo. Va a ser una carrera loca, hay que correr valientes y que no se vaya el grupo de los favoritos". Después, añade, será el propio recorrido el encargado de seleccionar la carrera: "Creo que pondrá a todos en su sitio haciendo una carrera de eliminación". Su temporada ya había dejado señales de crecimiento, con buenas actuaciones en pruebas como el ZLM Tour y Austria. Él siente que ha cumplido con el paso adelante que esperaba dar. "Igual sí que me hubiese gustado ganar, pero todavía quedan dos carreras muy importantes, como son el Mundial y el Europeo. El paso que esperaba es el que he dado y vamos poco a poco". A sus 19 años, tampoco tiene prisa por poner techo a su evolución. "Soy un corredor al que todavía le queda mucho por aprender y por mejorar. Estoy súper contento con la progresión que hemos hecho de un año a otro y ya mirando la evolución que creemos que vamos a tener, para seguir ese camino". Hay, sin embargo, una imagen que ya se permite imaginar: la de su primera victoria llegando en el escenario más grande. "Daría lo que fuera. Ahora vamos a descansar, a preparar bien y a mirar al viernes para que sea así: que mi primera victoria sea con el maillot de España y vistiéndome de campeón del mundo". En la selección española también respira optimismo. Mientras algunos compañeros hacen sus propias cuentas sobre el número de medallas que puede sumar España, Álvarez mantiene su pronóstico. "Ya lo dije antes de empezar. Creo que dije cinco o seis, así que lo mantengo". Y detrás de esa confianza aparece también el ambiente del equipo español. "Somos una familia. Ya nos conocemos de todos los años y estamos muy bien. Al final, cuando se trabaja a gusto, sale el resultado".

articles.title: Lionel Messi Reveals Argentina Jersey With Gold Numbers in Video Ahead of Final International Match
articles.summary: Lionel Messi is ending his international career for Argentina in style.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi is ending his international career for Argentina in style.

The soccer legend revealed the jersey he will wear for his final game with his country's national team that features gold numbers.

"Último partido… Una camiseta para toda la vida ❤️One last match… A jersey for a lifetime," he wrote on Instagram .

Messi's final game for Argentina will be a friendly against Benin on Oct. 6 at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. It will surely be a celebration of arguably the greatest career in the sport's history.

He is Argentina's all-time leading scorer and capped player and led the nation to a World Cup title in 2022.

articles.title: El ‘look’ más viral del Mundial: bici convencional, casco normal y gafas imposibles para 'retar' a Evenepoel
articles.standfirst: El ciclista de Guinea-Bissau Gil Gomes terminó último en la contrarreloj del Mundial, a casi 25 minutos de Evenepoel, pero su peculiar equipamiento y su dignidad sobre la bicicleta conquistaron Montreal
articles.summary: El ciclista de Guinea-Bissau Gil Gomes terminó último en la contrarreloj del Mundial, a casi 25 minutos de Evenepoel, pero su peculiar equipamiento y su dignidad sobre la bicicleta conquistaron Montreal
articles.body: En una disciplina donde cada detalle se estudia al milímetro para arañar unas décimas, Gil Landim Gomes apareció como una figura procedente de otro ciclismo. Uno más humilde, alejado de los túneles del viento, las bicicletas diseñadas exclusivamente para luchar contra el cronómetro y los llamativos cascos aerodinámicos. El representante de Guinea-Bissau acabó convirtiéndose, sin buscarlo, en uno de los protagonistas virales del Mundial de contrarreloj de Montreal. Su imagen en la rampa de salida llamó inmediatamente la atención. Gomes afrontó los 39,2 kilómetros del recorrido con una bicicleta de carretera convencional, un casco tradicional y unas particulares gafas que completaban un ‘look’ difícil de ignorar entre tanta tecnología. Frente a las sofisticadas máquinas de sus rivales, la suya parecía pertenecer a otra época. Las redes sociales tardaron muy poco en reparar en él. Su vestimenta y su material provocaron comentarios, comparaciones y numerosos mensajes de simpatía. Sin embargo, detrás de la anécdota estética había una historia mucho más profunda: la de un ciclista dispuesto a defender con orgullo los colores de su país pese a competir en evidente inferioridad de condiciones. Gomes completó el recorrido en 1h09:21, a una media de 33,9 kilómetros por hora. Fue el último clasificado, a casi 25 minutos del campeón Remco Evenepoel, pero llegó hasta la meta. No hubo gestos de frustración ni complejos. Pedaleó con serenidad, humildad y dignidad hasta finalizar una prueba concebida para premiar precisamente aquello de lo que él menos disponía: inversión, tecnología y medios. En Montreal, donde los grandes especialistas trataban de robarle segundos al reloj con bicicletas futuristas, Gomes libraba otra batalla. La suya no estaba contra Evenepoel ni contra el resto de corredores. Consistía simplemente en completar el recorrido y demostrar que Guinea-Bissau también tenía un lugar en el Mundial. El cronómetro asegura que fue el último. La imagen que dejó, sin embargo, cuenta algo diferente. Mientras otros peleaban por el arcoíris, la verdadera victoria de Gil Gomes fue estar allí, pedalear hasta el final y lograr que el mundo entero reparase durante unos minutos en los colores de su país.

articles.title: Alabama OC Calls Out Fans with Strong Quote for Booing Team Before Comeback Win vs. FSU
articles.summary: Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb didn't appreciate fans booing early during Saturday's 50-36 comeback win against Florida State.
articles.body:
Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb didn't appreciate fans booing early during Saturday's 50-36 comeback win against Florida State.

"We had some boo-birds," he told reporters during a press conference Monday. "I told the guys, I said, 'Shoot guys, if you'd have quit as fast as some of your fans, s--t, we wouldn't have won that game.' So I was proud of them. For a bunch of 19-year-olds to go out there and just [be down] 21-6 and not flinch, I was fired up."

The Crimson Tide found themselves trailing 21-6 in the second quarter before reeling off 20 straight points to end the first half. After punting on its first two drives, Alabama managed scoring drives on nine consecutive possessions before killing the clock to close the game.

Head coach Kalen DeBoer was also pleased with the team's resilience.

"Our team's shown that they got each other's backs, that's for sure," he told reporters. "We've seen that now multiple times when adversity has hit our football team. Proud of that part. Just got to go back to work and continue to improve, that's always the focus. It's about the next play, it's about the next game."

The 3-0 Crimson Tide will host South Carolina on Saturday.

articles.title: Andros Townsend: Being run over by pitch roller was 'terrifying'
articles.summary: Townsend says he was lucky to only escape from under the roller with a few "bumps and bruises".
articles.body:
Former England winger Andros Townsend has described the moment he was run over by a pitch roller in Thailand as "terrifying".

The 35‑year‑old former Tottenham, Luton and Crystal Palace forward, now with PT Prachuap in Thai League 1, was warming up for a match in Pattani on Saturday when a member of staff appeared to lose control of a heavy pitch roller.

Townsend's left leg briefly got stuck under the vehicle, but he was unhurt. He came off the bench late on in a 3-0 win.

Speaking about the incident for the first time on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored, Townsend said he was lucky to only escape from under the roller with a few "bumps and bruises".

"Every time I see it, I'm cringing, I'm in disbelief," he said.

"It's horrible to watch back and to see what could have been, thankfully I was fortunate I did manage to fall onto the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me."

Townsend run over by pitch roller in Thailand

Townsend, who won 13 caps for England, said that he did think it was strange to see two rollers either side of the pitch during the warm-up.

"I remember thinking to myself, 'I've never seen that before in my career, what are they doing?' But we got called to warm-up. Didn't think anything of it," he said.

"The next I saw him was when I was literally underneath him and thankfully no serious damage. A couple of bumps and bruises but managed to walk away unscathed, luckily."

Townsend, who has had numerous setbacks with injuries during his career, said the roller incident was "definitley not going to stop me from continuing".

"They (his team-mates) were very surprised that I continued the warm-up. They were telling me to go to the doctor," he said.

"It was quite heavy, but I was able to kind of lift [it], force it off me. So when it was completely on me, I was getting crushed a little bit.

"I was able to get my left arm up and relieve some of the pressure, and then I was able to get my team-mates around me who were able to lift it, and I was able to squeeze out but at that moment where it was crushing my left leg, it was quite terrifying, I must say."

Townsend was concerned his ankle and left knee, which have both been operated on, would be damaged in the incident.

He said: "I thought, either my left ankle was going to snap or my left knee is going to snap. I thought I was done. I was very fortunate that I was able to hobble away and recover within a few minutes."

The midfielder made light of the incident on Instagram, referencing one of his recent posts in which he compared a sun-drenched Thai away trip with previous visits to Stoke's Bet365 Stadium.

He wrote: "It turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all."

articles.title: Luis de la Fuente: "Hubo momentos que sí pensaba que Rodri ficharía por el Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador reconoció estar al tanto en el proceso del fichaje del medio por el Barcelona
articles.summary: El seleccionador reconoció estar al tanto en el proceso del fichaje del medio por el Barcelona
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente afronta su primera ventana de selecciones tras proclamarse campeón del mundo. El seleccionador español aprovechó su pasó por 'El Partidazo' de la cadena COPE para hablar de los nuevos retos del combinado nacional, la polémica del último derbi madrileño y otros temas de actualidad. “Lamine es muy respetuoso con Mbappé y me parece bien que se valoren ellos. Creo que lo dice con un tono divertido, de jugón...” “Creo que he hecho los mismos méritos que el resto de nominados. Se lo daría a un español, lo siento por Kompany. Es verdad que los seleccionadores tenemos menos posibilidades porque sólo tenemos una competición y este año era la más importante”. “Ha sido muy sencillo y muy fácil por ambas partes. Estoy en el mejor momento personal y profesional para asumir este reto. No le doy mucha importancia a lo económico, pero antes era de los peor pagados y ahora estoy en el otro lado". “Hace cuatro años hablaba de recuperar el espíritu de 2010, pues creo que lo hemos recuperado”. “Hubo momentos que sí pensaba que ficharía por el Real Madrid. Tengo buena relación con él y sabía cómo iban las conversaciones. Para mí, lo más importante es ver a esos grandes futbolistas en España. Si queremos seguir siendo los números uno hay que invertir en futbolistas españoles que, además, son los mejores”. “Había hablado con él e intenté convencerle, creo que tenía todo para seguir, pero a la vez respeté su decisión porque es una persona serena, sensata y cuando toma una decisión no es caprichosa. Sólo puedo darle las gracias”. “Creo que en la jugada de Kang in Lee le tenían que haber ayudado más al árbitro (desde el VAR). Tengo una relación fantástica con los árbitros y son muy buenos profesionales. Yo viajo por todo el mundo y creo que tenemos a los mejores árbitros” "Hay que darle una solución, la normalidad hay que devolvérsela ya. Es urgente".

articles.title: Marquette Men’s Soccer Preview: The 52nd Milwaukee Cup!
articles.summary: The Golden Eagles veer back into non-conference play after their Big East opener didn’t go their way.
articles.body:
For the first time in the half-century long history of the crosstown rivalry between Marquette men's soccer and Milwaukee men's soccer, Marquette secured the Milwaukee Cup traveling trophy for a fourth straight year. Marquette had never held the Cup for four years before that. Even with the series going allllll the way back to the first meeting in 1973, Marquette had never held it for four straight years. MU didn't even get to two straight until back-to-back 3-0 victories in 1982 and 1983, and a draw a year later was the first time they got to three straight. This is the kind of thing that happens when the all-time series history is tilted towards Milwaukee with Marquette's record standing at 13-31-6 against the Panthers.

Those were Marquette's only three runs of three straight years of holding the Cup.

And now, 2022-???, thanks to a 3-2 victory over on the East Side last season , powered by Tristan Ronnestad-Stevens' first career goal. Let's watch again, shall we?

Yes, if TRS hadn't come through there, Marquette still would have kept the Cup as the rules about draws means that the holder of the Cup keeps the Cup in that circumstance. But making series history with a win feels so much more compelling and important.

Can they do it again? Well, it's probably going to take a better performance than what we saw last time out against Georgetown. Yes, the Hoyas played their part in drubbing the Golden Eagles 3-0, but it certainly looked like Marquette was trying to drag Georgetown to hell in that match….. right up until GU scored 17 minutes in and then MU didn't have any idea what to do. That's been a problem regularly this year, with Marquette getting outshot in six of their eight matches. That hasn't particularly hurt Marquette yet, at least not terribly, as they're 5-2-1 overall with the losses coming against ranked opponents anyway. Part of "it hasn't hurt yet" is because Tomiwa Adewumi has scored eight goals on just 15 shots this season. You will, of course, not be surprised to find out that he was held without a shot in 66 minutes against Georgetown.

What's the plan from head coach David Korn and his staff to keep the Cup on Marquette's campus for another year? Guess we'll have to tune in on Tuesday and find out.

Match #9: vs Milwaukee Panthers (4-3-2, 2-1-0 Horizon League)

Date: Tuesday, September 22, 2026 Time: 6pm Central Location: Valley Fields, Milwaukee, Wisconsin Streaming: ESPN+ Live Stats: Stat Broadcast Bluesky Updates: @AnonymousEagle

A three match winning streak, including a pair of W's in Horizon League play, has turned around Milwaukee's record on the season so far. After a 3-2 loss to Wright State to start off conference action, the Panthers had dropped to just 1-3-2, and they had been shutout in three of those matches, two losses and a scoreless draw with Southern Indiana in their opener. Those two recent HL wins are great news for Milwaukee, as they were picked to finish sixth in the conference this season, but that comes at a price. Yes, they beat a Northern Illinois team that was picked third last time out…. but that Wright State loss? Yeah, the Raiders were picked to finish last. A mixed bag, perhaps.

The Panthers are about even with their opponents overall in terms of goals this season, 10 for and nine against. They're even in shots as well, 120 to 117 overall, so nearly dead even in average at about 13 attempts per contest. Milwaukee's biggest problem has been shot selection, or at the very least accuracy. They're only putting 35% of shots on frame, while their opponents are up over 40%. That tilts the advantage towards the opponent at least in terms of quality chances, but again: Slim lead at putting it in the net.

There are eight different goal scorers for UWM so far this year, with Jack Wagner and Praise Ogwu coming in as the only guys with two goals. Wagner has the team lead in points at five as he has an assist as well. The junior defender from Delafield has scored both goals in Horizon League play, including finding the net last time out against NIU for the opening goal less than eight minutes in. While those two are the most successful players in terms of scoring, Roy Nozawa is the guy that's leading Milwaukee's attack in shots with 17. Nozawa has only started three matches this season, and he's played less than 25 minutes in each of the last two matches for the Panthers. Keeping an eye out for him subbing in will be a key detail for Marquette's defense.

As for Milwaukee's defense, Filip Dostanic and Carson Pridie have split the goalkeeping duties right down the middle as much as you can with nine matches in the books. It seems likely that Marquette will get Pridie on Tuesday night, as he's started the last three and five of the last six. On top of that, he's also the better netminder in terms of stats. He's allowing just 0.80 goals per 90 minutes and stopping 85% of shots on frame. Dostanic isn't too bad on save percentage at .750, but his goals-against average is way up at 1.25. If head coach Kris Kelderman is devoted to what direction he's been going lately, then sticking with Pridie is the obvious choice.

articles.title: Following Florida flop in 2025, No. 1 Texas looks for a better SEC start at Tennessee
articles.summary: Texas opens SEC play on Saturday when it travels to Tennessee. This game will be the conference opener for both schools. Winning a SEC title won't be easy, b...
articles.body:
Over the first three weeks of the season, Texas football beat Texas State and UTSA and recorded a memorable win over Ohio State .

No. 1 Texas opens SEC play this weekend when it travels to No. 14 Tennessee , the conference opener for both schools.

Winning an SEC championship won't be easy. On Sunday, Associated Press voters reserved 10 of the 25 spots in its poll for SEC teams: No. 1 Texas, No. 2 Georgia, No. 4 Ole Miss, No. 8 Alabama , No. 10 LSU , No. 14 Tennessee, No. 19 Missouri , No. 21 Florida , No. 23 Texas A&M and No. 24 Mississippi State . Two more SEC teams ( Kentucky and Oklahoma ) received votes.

"Here's the deal, we're starting SEC play," said UT coach Steve Sarkisian, who has seven currently-ranked opponents on his nine-game conference schedule. "I've said it time and time again, from top to bottom, anybody can beat anybody, and I think that's the challenge of our conference is being mentally and physically prepared to play week in and week out. For us this week, it's no different."

Is the SEC opener a must-win game for Texas?

Mathematically speaking, the loser of Saturday's UT-UT showdown won't be removed from the conference championship conversation. But historically speaking, it has been tougher for teams that lost their conference opener to contend for a spot in the SEC title game. The last SEC champion that started 0-1 in conference was Alabama in 2015. And the SEC hasn't had a runner-up that lost its conference opener since 2011.

Starting conference play with a loss shrinks a team's margin of error. Last year, Texas had to play catch-up last year after losing its SEC opener at Florida. The Longhorns finished with a 6-2 mark in conference play, but weren't in the first-place mix in a league that had four 7-1 teams.

"The goal is always to win the game," Texas defensive tackle Hero Kanu said Monday. "Florida is behind us. We've got them later on in the schedule (this season), but yeah, the goal is to win."

The 2025 Florida game also was brought up at Sarkisian's news conference. Texas was stunned last year in Gainesville by the Gators , who were weeks away from firing their head coach. In a 29-21 loss , Texas committed two turnovers and allowed 457 yards of offense.

"I get it. We didn't play well at Florida last year, but we are 13-3 in SEC play," Sarkisian said. "I'm very confident in our ability to go on the road and play well."

Texas begins SEC play this year against Tennessee

The last two years, Texas got its feet wet in SEC play against Mississippi State and Florida teams that both failed to qualify for bowl games. The Volunteers, on the other hand, are undefeated, ranked and also trying to remain in the SEC title picture. This summer, Tennessee was listed eighth in a SEC preseason poll in which Texas was No. 2.

So far this season, Tennessee is averaging 47.7 points and 510.3 yards. The Volunteers held Furman and Kennesaw State to under 10 points while two turnovers were forced in a 21-point win over Georgia Tech . Texas safety Jelani McDonald said he's looking forward to the matchup between the Vols' running game and Texas' physicality. And center Connor Robertson wants to see what the Longhorns' run game can do as well.

"Really good defense. Really good defensive coordinator," Robertson said. "A lot of production, especially in their front seven. They've got some experienced guys. They've got some new faces, obviously some transfers and stuff, but we've played against (Tennessee defensive coordinator Jim Knowles when he was at Ohio State ), and it's just a great opportunity for us to go out on Saturday and have a good game."

articles.title: Real Madrid the ‘team that has benefited most’ from referees, says Barcelona legend Carles Rexach
articles.summary: The former coach has no sympathy for Los Blancos.
articles.body:
Barcelona legend Carles Rexach says that Real Madrid are the "team that has benefited the most" from referees throughout history.

Real Madrid TV regularly complain about referees and were at it again after Sunday's derby defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Manager Jose Mourinho also criticized the match officials after the defeat, but Rexach feels Los Blancos have traditionally seen results go in their favor.

"Throughout history, the team that has benefited the most, not only in Spain but in Europe, has been Real Madrid. In my time playing, we always came away with our losses," he told 2Cat program 'El cafè d'idees' "I thought that with the VAR system, which I was initially very much in favor of—because you can't have a goal awarded when the ball hasn't crossed the line, and before they couldn't disallow it—I thought this advantage of VAR would be more effective. "But if before there was a problem with the referee and the linesmen, now there are the same ones plus the VAR officials, and we haven't made much progress; we're in the same situation as before."

"Throughout history, the team that has benefited the most, not only in Spain but in Europe, has been Real Madrid. In my time playing, we always came away with our losses," he told 2Cat program 'El cafè d'idees'

"I thought that with the VAR system, which I was initially very much in favor of—because you can't have a goal awarded when the ball hasn't crossed the line, and before they couldn't disallow it—I thought this advantage of VAR would be more effective.

"But if before there was a problem with the referee and the linesmen, now there are the same ones plus the VAR officials, and we haven't made much progress; we're in the same situation as before."

Sunday's defeat has left Madrid down in fourth place in the table in Spain, six points behind Barcelona after the first seven games.

articles.title: NaLyssa Smith was rolling before injury that turned her into cheerleader for Aces' repeat quest
articles.summary: NaLyssa Smith was playing some of her best basketball when she suffered a season-ending non-contact left leg injury Aug. 23.  Now she has to sit and watch he...
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. (AP) — NaLyssa Smith was playing some of her best basketball when she suffered a season-ending non-contact left leg injury Aug. 23.

Now she has to sit and watch her Las Vegas Aces teammates try to repeat as WNBA champions and win their fourth title in five years.

"You never plan on having an injury," Smith said Monday. "You always plan on just having a better year every single year. so it's been tough. But I've been surrounded by nothing but love and grace."

Smith took a lot of pressure off four-time MVP A'ja Wilson by giving the Aces a key second weapon in the post. She averaged 11.8 points and 6.4 rebounds over 37 games at the time of her injury and led the league in field goal percentage at 63.8%.

"I feel like this has probably been one of my best years so far," said Smith, in her fifth season. "So it's unfortunate it came to an end so quickly, but now that I know I can (play well), I can build on it."

Smith said Wilson has kept in regular contact with her and that coach Becky Hammon shared how she overcame her own injury problems as a Hall of Fame player.

Losing Smith was a big blow to the Aces' title chances, though they went into Monday third in the standings with two games left. Las Vegas is a consensus second choice to win the championship behind Minnesota .

"I feel like every athlete, you're going to go through something, whether that's a hard time in your life, whether that is losing somebody in a family, whether that's just being depressed because of basketball," Smith said. "I've gone through many trials and tribulations, so this is just another stepping stone."

articles.title: Zach Ertz is 11 catches from setting Eagles' franchise record
articles.summary: Zach Ertz returns to Philadelphia needing 11 receptions to pass Harold Carmichael as the Eagles’ all-time leader
articles.body:
Zach Ertz's return to the Philadelphia Eagles gives the Super Bowl hero an opportunity to finish some unfinished business. Ertz is signing with Philadelphia's practice squad after Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL during Sunday's victory over Tennessee. Beyond helping the Eagles navigate Goedert's absence, Ertz is positioned to make franchise history.

Ertz recorded 579 receptions during his first stint in Philadelphia. Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver Harold Carmichael owns the franchise record with 589, according to Pro Football Reference . That leaves Ertz 10 receptions away from tying Carmichael and 11 from becoming the Eagles' all-time leader. Ertz already holds Philadelphia's single-season receptions record after catching 116 passes in 2018. He also ranks fifth in franchise history with 6,267 receiving yards and is the organization's most productive tight end.

His place in Eagles history was secure before this reunion. Ertz caught the go-ahead touchdown in Philadelphia's Super Bowl LII victory over New England and earned three consecutive Pro Bowl selections from 2017 through 2019. The Eagles initially brought Ertz back because they needed an experienced receiving option behind Goedert . The practice-squad signing gives him time to prepare before potentially joining the active roster.

If Ertz can contribute during Goedert's absence, he could do more than help Philadelphia survive an early-season injury. He could complete his return by taking possession of one of the most significant records in franchise history.

articles.title: Ryan Silverfield: Arkansas ‘absolutely’ working to improve resources for football program
articles.summary: Ahead of Arkansas’ Week 3 game against Georgia, the university board announced plans to conduct a review of the athletics department and resources for the fo...
articles.body:
Ahead of Arkansas' Week 3 game against Georgia , the university board announced plans to conduct a review of the athletics department and resources for the football program. Speaking with reporters Monday, Razorbacks head coach Ryan Silverfield said the school is "absolutely" working to improve in that area.

As part of the resolution, approved unanimously by the Arkansas board of trustees, school president Jay Silveria to lead a comprehensive review of the athletics department's competitiveness. It also paved the way for Silveria to look at ways to improve the resources at the football program's disposal.

Arkansas athletics director Hunter Yurachek told ABC's Taylor McGregor he has not yet spoken with the board or Silveria about the statement. When asked about whether the Razorbacks had the resources this year, Silverfield supported they did, and he noted the plans to keep have even more available.

"I like our roster," Silverfield said . "I like the young men we have. We're going to go out there and fight and compete. Our plan is we're going to bring our absolute best every single week. Are we going to continue to work to improve our resources here at the University of Arkansas? Absolutely.

"I also knew that this job wasn't going to be easy. We talked about it when I first got here that there's a reason why we've only won one Power Four home game in the last three years. But it's my job to fix that. I make no doubts and no excuses and no explanations that we will get this fixed and we will get this turned around in the right direction because we have a bunch of guys that believe and are going to keep fighting. Our job is to continue to improve the resources to better give ourselves an opportunity each and every time we take take the field."

Fan frustration has been building at Arkansas as Silverfield goes through Year 1 in Fayetteville. Additionally, separate from the university board's statement, The Athletic reported the Razorbacks have the lowest roster cost in the SEC at between $22 million and $25 million.

Silverfield said fundraising efforts took place this offseason and he took part. While he noted the timing of his hire to replace Sam Pittman meant he wasn't around for the discussions about this year's recruiting class, his goal is to stay aligned with the athletics department when it comes to resources.

"I'm hopeful that everybody's understanding of where we need to get to. … I think a lot of the fundraising is for the betterment of the program, wherever that may end up," Silverfield said. "That's to be determined. A lot of that's out of my hands and we'll figure it out.

"Again, my whole deal is alignment and making sure everybody understands where we want this program to be and where, realistically, we may be. However that money is getting spent and what timetable, that is to be determined. That is currently, right now, out of my control."

articles.title: Colts decision to play it safe in overtime against Chiefs winds up proving costly for Steichen
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen chose the safe play in overtime Sunday night.  After deciding to start overtime by kicking off, holding the Chiefs to...
articles.body:
INDIANPOOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen chose the safe play in overtime Sunday night.

It proved costly then and it could prove costly later if the playoffs are involved.

After deciding to start overtime by kicking off, holding the Chiefs to a field goal and then moving inside the Chiefs 20-yard line, Steichen made three conservative play calls before settling for the tying field goal and giving two-time league MVP and three-time Super Bowl MVP Patrick Mahomes one last chance to win the game.

Mahomes quickly moved Kansas City (2-0) into position for Harrison Butker 's 40-yard field goal as time expired for a second straight overtime loss at Arrowhead Stadium.

Afterward, Steichen explained he wanted the Colts' top offensive playmaker, Jonathan Taylor , to close out the game.

"We were trying to score there," Steichen said Monday. "The thought process was J.T. there on that, we had four downs and then you had the second down situation. I thought we could pop a run, get it to third-and-manageable and then, you know, you have two downs to go for it. It didn't work out in that situation, and any time you don't get the results you want, obviously, you second-guess things."

Steichen considered going for the winning touchdown on fourth-and-8 from the Chiefs 15. He kept the offense on the field, hoping to get a favorable look from Kansas City's defense, and when it didn't happen, Indy took a delay of game penalty and kicked the 38-yard field goal with 3:11 to go.

Mahomes responded by doing what he does best — producing game-winning drives.

The result: Indy (0-2) extended the league's longest active losing streak to nine, and the decisions won't help Steichen's stock in a season team co-owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has described as critical for Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard.

Some Colts fans compared it to Steichen's decision to punt from his 40 on the first possession of overtime last November at Kansas City. Mahomes did the same thing then, leading the Chiefs on an 87-yard drive to set up Butker's 27-yard game winning kick.

But whether it was last season or Sunday night, Steichen did what he thought was right and he didn't back down from those decisions Monday.

"It's a results-based, a results-driven league and if you don't get the results you want, obviously, you're going to look back on some things that didn't go your way," he said. "That's part of it, that's the NFL. So in those situations, we've just got to go out and do our job the best we can do, to go find a way to win."

Josh Downs . Taylor had another terrific game with 132 total yards rushing and two TD runs, but Downs delivered while being pressed into the No. 1 receiver's role because of Alec Pierce 's heal injury. Downs caught seven of the nine passes thrown his way for 72 yards and helped give the offense some much-needed balance.

Tackling. Indy has given up 74 points in its first two games and has allowed more than 500 yards in each game, which ranks among the worst in league history. The problem in Week 1 seemed to be misalignments in part because safety Camryn Bynum was the on-field play-caller. The problem Sunday night, they needed extra tacklers to corral RBs Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson or TE Travis Kelce .

Laquon Treadwell . The receiver nearly became the goat of the game when he appeared to fumble a 48-yard completion that the Chiefs recovered. But a replay review overturned the fumble and nearly turned Treadwell into the hero. That wasn't his only contribution. He had a 10-yard reception on Indy's first TD drive and drew a 26-yard pass interference penalty to set up a field goal.

Keenan Allen . The six-time Pro Bowler finished with just one reception for 5 yards despite being targeted five times. But it wasn't just the numbers. Allen failed to wrestle the ball away from Kristian Fulton on Indy's second series, which led to a Chiefs TD. He also failed to catch two third down passes.

Pierce did not return after leaving in the first half, and Steichen said Monday that the X-rays came back negative, but that he did aggravate something in the same leg he had ankle surgery in March. CB Charvarius Ward left in the second half with groin tightness, but Steichen said he would know more about Ward's availability later this week.

191 — The Colts defense has allowed 1,029 yards through games — 191 yards more than every team other than the Detroit Lions , who have allowed 915 yards this season. Carolina ranks 30th with 838 yards, entering Monday.

The offense and special teams looked markedly better in Week 2, and the defense also improved despite giving up so much yardage against yet another league MVP. But it's still not good enough. Indy must continue to work on the basics — tackling, coverage and proper alignments — to avoid yet another loss against the winless Texans .
